title: Verify input restartability before using a two-pass iterator algorithm
applies_when: A helper takes a generic lazy iterator and counts, validates or builds metadata in one pass, then rereads that same input to produce output. Also check variadic zero/one-input cases where nominally distinct first/last roles become the same iterator. Channel, file, cursor and generator adapters may consume an external resource rather than restart it.
lesson: Inspect the actual producer, not just the iterator type or tests built from slices. Compose the public helper with an existing one-shot adapter and compare unchanged source against the repair. In lo at 5c6ddcb, FindUniquesBy counts keys then rereads collection, while ChannelToSeq drains a channel; unique values disappear on the second pass. For finite uniqueness filtering, retain first occurrences with a key-to-index map, invalidate repeated keys and emit the remaining values in original order after one traversal. A second supported boundary is unary Intersect/IntersectBy: lists[len(lists)-1] and lists[0] are identical when there is one input, so building the last-input set drains the first input. Delegate that case to the existing streaming Uniq/UniqBy instead of adding a value buffer; leave zero/multiple-input paths alone. Keep state inside each result invocation so restartable inputs stay restartable. Test single-use and restartable producers, laziness, early break, named iterator types and non-comparable payloads with comparable transformed keys.
avoid_when: An explicit API may require restartable input or intentionally re-evaluate it; a repeated call alone is not a bug. GPU producer/consumer scheduler advances can partition work rather than consume the same stream. Buffering values changes memory needs and must be disclosed, especially when keys are much smaller than payloads. A uniqueness-before-yield contract already requires finite input; do not silently materialize arbitrary infinite streams. A local fix and native tests do not establish upstream acceptance, portable performance, improved Scout yield or a prospective routing benefit.

evidence.note: Go's iterator convention explicitly permits single-use iterators backed by consumed data. The type alone does not promise restartability.
Pinned FindUniquesBy traverses collection twice and transforms values in both passes; its public contract does not require restartable input.
The same library's ChannelToSeq ranges directly over its channel, providing a concrete supported one-shot producer rather than an invented adversarial iterator.

Public fork repair and focused regressions retain ordering, single traversal and early break. Independently tested on Linux and real Windows; publication/upstream acceptance and performance are not inferred from this commit.

The first/last iterator roles alias for one argument in both Intersect variants. This is the producer-consumption mechanism, not a requirement that every multiple-input alias be cloned or an upstream-acceptance claim.
Existing tests explicitly support a single input and duplicate removal, but construct restartable slice-backed iterators. Their presence does not cover a single-use producer.

Separate unary Intersect/By repair delegates to streaming Uniq/UniqBy without buffering the whole input. Public regressions cover ChannelToSeq, transform counts, laziness/early break, named restartable inputs and zero/multiple-input controls. Independently validated on Linux and Windows; an open PR is not upstream acceptance or evidence of prospective routing gains.
